plain_what: During training, a teacher marks which earlier words hold the value the question asks for and which hold other stated values. The model is rewarded for putting its attention on the right ones. It targets the failure 'found a value, but the wrong one', and nothing about how answers are produced changes at serving time.
how_it_works: For a query whose next token belongs to a stated value, the training data carries labels: source positions that hold the asked value (bound) and positions that hold the other stated values (competing). The geometric read has per-head attention weights over earlier positions. Let m_bound be the attention mass on bound positions. The loss on the best-binding head is -log(m_bound + 1e-6) (READ_SUPERVISION_FLOOR = 1e-6) with weight W (0.1 in the keeper, 0.5 in the first test), added to the language loss. Competing mass is monitored, and in one variant penalised with 0.5*relu(m_competing - 0.03). The labels never touch a hidden state or a logit, so the served network is unchanged; only the read learns to separate values. It is applied to a late read layer (layer 8 in a stack whose reads are layers 2, 5 and 8) and from step 0 of the fine-tune. The exact-by-construction variant (read_lineage = phase_bind) gives each value a fixed phase or lineage tag so binding is exact rather than learned; a random-SO(4) lineage is the control. Labels come from a sidecar file produced with the dialogue corpus.
geometry: Acts on the Lorentz-score R4-state read; the phase-binding variant uses fixed (snapped) phases and a ReadLineage tag, with a random SO(4) lineage as control. The core supervised form uses no special geometric object.

status_reason: Met its mechanism target and moved the headline in the one form tested (3 seeds from step 0: wrong-value 47 -> 30/120, memory 57 -> 65/120, docs/labs/read-binding-powered-2026-10-11/README.md), but that read is a float softmax attention, inactive under D23/D30/D32. It has never been tried on any discrete or geometric read.
reopen_conditions: Re-register as an offline float sheet under D37 on a read that is not a softmax attention (a rank-table, Flock or Relation read), as a separately scanned module with an integer export and a reported export gap; fresh TEST FITNESS: FIT and owner release.
Or port the signal to the D32 discrete read (Route, Flock, Relation): the discrete analogue of bound versus competing mass, supervised from the start of training.

Fair-test conditions: supervise from the start (not a late bolt-on), at least 3 seeds, at least 120 memory rows, a matched W=0 control, held-out bound and competing mass, and a head-ablation check that the bound head drives the answer; bar of +5/40-equivalent over the control.

Change the supervision rather than its length or its sharpness: both the 16,000-step and margin variants decoupled the masses from the panel; per-head supervision or routing the output through the binding head are the named candidates.

rule_compat.D11: Training-only signal: the labels never enter the network and nothing of the loss exists at serving time, so it adds no served operation. The tested read had no D11 served form.
rule_compat.D23: Violates in the tested form: the loss itself has no softmax (it is -log of an attention mass) but the mass comes from a softmax attention read (docs/labs/attention-state-2026-10-18/README.md: 'it is a softmax read'). The tested runs are preserved as inactive evidence.
rule_compat.D30: The 29M float stack it trained is a dense matmul stack; the signal needs a matmul-free read to be re-registered.
rule_compat.D32_D37: Not on the D32 discrete path. Float training is legal offline under D37, so the signal itself is admissible if attached to a lawful geometric read and exported to an integer artifact.

never_tested: Read-binding supervision on any discrete or geometric read (Route, Flock, Relation) or any read that is not a softmax attention.
Per-head supervision (every head) or routing the output through the binding head, named after the 16,000-step result.
Pairing the binding with the pointer so that bound positions feed the copy distribution directly.
Held-out bound and competing mass: the masses reported are train-side.
At least 120 memory rows per seed: every panel has 40 memory rows (the standing declared deviation).
Binding labels on a model pretrained with the mechanism (all runs are fine-tunes of one 29M base); transfer to fresh combinations is unmeasured for this mechanism.
A pre-registered fresh-draw transfer number for the KEEP (D22 section 4).
failed_only_on_configuration: #2155 (W=0.1/0.5, one seed, late bolt-on, 40-row panel): met its own target; the headline moved by one row, inside the +/-2-3 row noise. D22 reopened it.
214M arm P vs Q (29/40 vs 31/40): a float pointer stack on a different panel and recipe; counted as a negative of that configuration.
Competing-mass margin: sharper separation of the same read left the panel flat; closes the hinge, not the idea.
Phase binding: exactness of the same quantity cost 13.4x wall time and lost rows; says exact lineage tagging as built is a bad route, not that binding is.
Longer training (16,000 steps): closes the budget lever only.
Binding-dense data lever: more binding examples in the data is not the supervision.
open_questions: Is the lever 'bound mass on the right value' or something the masses do not capture? The masses kept improving while the panel gain stopped growing.
Supervise every head, or route the output through the binding head?
Pair it with the pointer so bound positions feed the copy distribution?
Phase or lineage tagging of values (exact binding) instead of learned mass, in a form that is cheap (the tested form cost 13.4x)?
What is the discrete analogue of bound and competing mass on a ternary-gate read?
evidence: docs/integration/DECISIONS.md (D21, D22 section 5(e), D23, D30, D37)
related: pointer-key: the copy head found not to be the answer path; binding acts on the read it bypasses
exact-memory: the exact-address alternative to learning which value a read binds to
flock-read and relation-read: the softmax-free reads a re-registration would supervise
route-read: the invariant-addressed read that answers 'address instead of search' without a mass to supervise
admission: the measured ceiling on what any read can reach, which supervision cannot raise
